subject: Re: ACME MSA — damages exclusion language and cap carve-outs
messages:
From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com, legal@acme.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MSA redlines — damages exclusion

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for sending over the MSA. Our legal team flagged the damages section — specifically the exclusion for consequential, special, incidental and punitive damages. They prefer a one-way exclusion (protecting Acme) and are proposing the following: "Redwood shall be liable for direct damages only; Acme shall not be liable to Redwood for any consequential, incidental, special, punitive or exemplary damages."

They also requested removal of certain carve-outs (e.g., for confidentiality breaches) and asked that the contract not cap liability for IP infringement. Attached are our redlines (ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx).

Can you confirm Redwood's position? We're trying to get internal sign-off this week.

Best,
Marta
Marta Silva
Senior Counsel, Acme Industries

Attachments: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx, 73KB)

From: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@acme.com>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — damages exclusion

Marta — thanks for the redlines and the quick turnaround.

High level: Redwood prefers a mutual damages exclusion for consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, with limited carve-outs for (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct, (ii) IP infringement, and (iii) breach of confidentiality. We also typically keep a liability cap tied to the order form fees (12 months revenue) rather than removing the cap for IP claims.

To move forward quickly: would Acme consider (A) mutual exclusion language, (B) preserving carve-outs above, and (C) an explicit carve-in for IP infringement where the cap either increases for that claim or is uncapped if injunctive relief is sought? I'm attaching a short summary of proposed language and an SLA matrix so we can scope severity-based remedies.

Proposed sample (for discussion):
"Neither party shall be liable to the other for any consequential, incidental, indirect, special, punitive or exemplary damages, including but not limited to lost profits, loss of business, or loss of data, arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, regardless of the form of action, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), strict liability, or otherwise. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this exclusion shall not apply to (a) liabilities resulting from a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) breach of the confidentiality obligations set forth in this Agreement, and (c) claims of intellectual property infringement, for which remedies shall include injunctive relief and damages subject to the liability cap set forth in the Order Form (or higher as mutually agreed)."

If that language is a non-starter, happy to jump on a call with your counsel.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_summary.pdf (pdf, 45KB); SLA_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)

Laura / Aditya — forwarding Acme's position. They pushed for a one-way exclusion in their favor and asked us to remove the confidentiality/IP carve-outs.

We need a quick legal position: 1) Are we comfortable with mutual exclusion plus the three carve-outs I proposed? 2) If they insist on one-way, what's the recommended commercial trade (cap increase, higher SLA, credits)? 3) Any mandatory language we should insist on (e.g., gross negligence, fraud exceptions)?

Meeting window: tomorrow 10–11am PT or 2–3pm PT.

—Tessa

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — damages exclusion

Tessa / team — quick read from legal: we should not accept a one-way exclusion that removes carve-outs for confidentiality/IP. Key points:

- Mutual exclusion is standard and reduces precedent risk. A one-way exclusion could expose Redwood to uncapped consequential liabilities while protecting Acme — unacceptable.
- Carve-outs we must keep: (1) willful misconduct/gross negligence; (2) breach of confidentiality (customer data); (3) IP infringement (we can accept injunctive relief but damages should remain within the cap or a pre-agreed higher cap).
- Commercial levers if Acme insists: increase cap from 12 months to 18 months, add SLA financial credits up to X% of monthly fees, and include a narrow carve-out for qualifying regulatory fines (if they insist).
- Suggested revision to sample language (short):
"Neither party will be liable for consequential, special, incidental, punitive or exemplary damages (including lost profits), except to the extent arising from (a) a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, (b) breach of confidentiality obligations, or (c) claims for actual intellectual property infringement, for which remedies shall include injunctive relief and damages subject to the limitations of liability described in the Order Form."

Recommend we offer the mutual exclusion + (i) keep the three carve-outs; (ii) propose an 18-month cap if they insist on one-way or removal of carve-outs; (iii) require an explicit indemnity for third-party IP suits (if they ask to carve IP into the cap, we should limit the indemnity scope).

Happy to discuss on the call.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@acme.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com, legal@acme.com
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — damages exclusion

Tessa — appreciate the quick legal input. Our team is concerned about Redwood's potential exposure and operational risk. They will consider a mutual exclusion only if Redwood increases liability cap to 24 months revenue and accepts a limited warranty carve-in for data loss events.

Alternatively, we can accept mutual language if Redwood agrees to: (1) higher cap (24 months for direct damages), and (2) express warranty remedies for outage-related losses (SLA credits). We are not comfortable with uncapped IP damages; we can accept injunctive relief only.

Can Redwood confirm whether the 24-month cap is workable or whether you can make a concession on SLA credits in lieu of a cap increase?

Best,
Marta

From: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@acme.com>, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 9 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME MSA redlines — damages exclusion

Marta / team — quick commercial reply from Redwood: we cannot remove carve-outs for confidentiality/IP or accept a one-way exclusion. That exposes our customers and sets bad precedent.

We can offer the following package to close: 
- Mutual exclusion language (see Laura's suggested wording).
- Liability cap: increase to 18 months of order-form fees for this enterprise deal (goodwill concession).
- SLA: enhanced credits for uptime below thresholds (SLA_matrix.xlsx attached) and a short period of elevated incident support for the first 12 months.
- IP: Injunctive relief is acceptable, and we will keep damages for IP claims within the 18-month cap; Redwood will provide an IP indemnity limited to third-party infringement claims where we have control and indemnify costs capped at the liability cap.

If Acme can accept that package, we can finalize the MSA and start the DocuSign flow today. If Acme insists on 24 months or one-way exclusion, we'd need legal approval for an exception and likely additional pricing to compensate.

Next steps: Marta — can you confirm whether Acme will accept mutual exclusion + 18-month cap + SLA credits so we can route for signature?

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
